detailed_description:
The target video is a living sumi ink painting in <Subject 2>: every stroke keeps its wet brushed texture as it moves, ink flows and drips like real liquid ink on paper, and the hairline moon and cloud outlines stay thin, clean and steady.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>. The black cat holds her crouch for a heartbeat, haunches shifting and the tip of her tail twitching, then drives off the brush stroke of ink with her hind legs in slow motion. Her body uncoils and stretches upward on a rising diagonal toward the moon, front paws lifting off the ground and reaching up, her fur rippling with the force of the push. Her tail sweeps down and back behind her, trailing a long ribbon of wet ink that sheds drops onto the paper. Every frame keeps her rough dry-brush ink texture, ragged wispy fur edges and white slash highlights; she is never a smooth, flat cartoon shape, and her motion is weighty and real, like a slow-motion wildlife shot. The camera begins a slow, smooth tilt up, lagging slightly behind her like a real camera operator, the ground stroke sinking toward the bottom edge and more of the moon coming into view at the upper right. The camera is still tilting up and she is still rising as the shot ends on <Picture 2>. No cut or transition occurs.

overall_soundscape:
Her claws rasp across the paper as she pushes off, a soft deep thump marks the launch, and a low rush of air follows. Wet ink drops patter onto the paper behind her tail.
